To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SMILLE is a system for enhancing second language acquisition by means of input enhancements that can be freely chosen from online documents.

SMILLE is able to detect 107 types of grammatical information with an average precision of 87% and an average recall of 80%, and that the system is able to provide a user experience that engages the learner in the process of acquiring a language.

SMILLE is an innovative system that uses NLP techniques to provide input enhancement to online texts, thus potentially enhancing second language acquisition, in a way that is engaging for the user and reflects the user’s interests, by means of a user interface that is simple and intuitive to use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of a system that provides an input-enhanced environment for second language learning.
the development of an online system that provides input enhancement for a given text.
the development and evaluation of a system that can enhance online documents, chosen by a user, with grammatical information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SMILLE is a promising system that can help second language learners in acquiring the grammatical structures of the target language, and that can be further improved in terms of the accuracy of the grammar analysis, and in terms of the input enhancement techniques.

the system is able to detect grammatical structures in online documents with an overall precision of approximately 87% and that it is able to enhance the salience of those structures, which is a crucial step towards the development of an effective and engaging learning tool for language acquisition.
the system can be a useful tool for enhancing the learning of second language grammar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SMILLE system is capable of providing input enhancements to online documents, which are based on grammatical information, and which are chosen by the users.
the system is able to identify a wide range of grammatical structures and enhance them with the use of visual and auditory input enhancements.
we have developed a system that can detect grammatical structures in a given online text, and can highlight them to the user, in the hope of increasing their intake of grammatical structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the system could be used for enhancing the salience of grammatically correct sentences in online documents.
the system could be used for enhancing the salience of grammar in online texts and for increasing the user’s intake of grammatical information.
SMILLE can be used for enhancing second language acquisition by providing input to the user that is enriched with metalinguistic grammatical information.
